title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation call per intent reused for both episodes) we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated template-driven repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial generations + 1 repair). Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. We did not execute the preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast; the reported confirmatory estimand applies to the synthetic/emulation partition only. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the submission evidence bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps), promising more rapid drafting of device CLI sequences and intent-driven automation. Stochastic generation, however, creates operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties can produce unsafe or non-functional device changes. Prior survey and empirical work documents LLM feasibility for draft configurations while highlighting the continuing need for deterministic verification or human oversight [1],[2].

A common architectural response is to interpose a deterministic validator between generation and acceptance and, optionally, perform bounded automated repair — a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pattern — which accepts only validator-passed candidates or attempts limited repair when mechanically verifiable defects are detected. GVR pipelines reduce mechanically verifiable error classes (syntax, ordering, straightforward local-policy violations) in prior reports but leave open how large the marginal benefit of such guardrails is when modern LLM outputs already conform to the validator encodings under constrained tasks [3],[4].

This paper reports a sealed, preregistered paired experiment designed to isolate the marginal verifier+single-repair effect when the same initial candidate is reused across conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics). By design the experiment measures only the validator-and-repair marginal effect on identical model outputs rather than conflating generation variability across conditions. Our principal contribution is an artifact-grounded quantification of that marginal verifier-detected improvement (and its statistical bounds) for a constrained NetOps task set.
sections.related_work:
Work on LLMs for NetOps and intent-driven configuration has grown rapidly. Several studies evaluate LLMs’ ability to synthesize configuration fragments and intent translations in emulation and controlled settings and note the need for verification layers [1],[2]. Empirical and engineering reports emphasize the utility of deterministic verification tools (e.g., forwarding/reachability checkers and configuration analyzers) as validators in GVR pipelines [3],[4]. Research from program repair and generate-and-validate literature documents that interposing deterministic checks plus constrained repair can raise mechanically verifiable correctness while not guaranteeing broader semantic correctness [5],[7].

Security analyses of prompt-injection and indirect-injection attacks also recommend filtering and validation layers to mitigate operational compromise, emphasizing that adaptive attackers remain a practical unresolved threat in complex pipelines [6]. Our study differs by (i) using a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics that isolates the validator/repair marginal effect on identical generated candidates, (ii) reporting reconciled provider-call accounting at the stage level, and (iii) archiving complete validator traces and reconciliation artifacts to support auditing and reproducibility.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 and specified a confirmatory paired design with N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration froze the single-repair policy, exclusion and contamination rules, the analysis methods (exact McNemar two-sided and paired-bootstrap percentile CIs), and the maximum model-call budget. The preregistration artifact SHA-256 is 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics (confirmatory design). Under the registered shared_initial_candidate design exactly one initial model-generation call was produced per intent and that same generated candidate was reused for both episodes (baseline and guarded); no independent first-pass generation per condition was performed. This isolates the marginal effect of deterministic validation and the single permitted repair on an identical candidate. Provider-call reconciliation records hosted_model_call_event_count = 251 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1} reflecting 250 shared initial-generation calls plus a single repair-stage invocation.

Task bank and constraints. A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 250 constrained intent tasks. Each task encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and a difficulty label (medium/hard/very_hard). Tasks exercised workflow constraints representative of common NetOps patterns (make-before-break uplink switchover, paired-link atomic MTU changes, safe access transfer) and enforced protected interfaces that must not be modified. The full task manifest and representative payloads are archived in the evidence bundle.

Model and pipeline. The declared model for initial generation was gpt-5-mini. For each intent we executed one shared initial generation call. The guarded pipeline submitted the shared candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5, which implements full_intent_constraint_validation: parsing CLI sequences, checking required_sequence ordering and workflow constraints, producing a final_state snapshot, and returning a boolean valid flag plus diagnostic fields (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes). When the validator returned valid = false the pipeline was permitted up to one automated, template-driven repair and a single re-submission; repairs were restricted to deterministic syntactic and ordering fixes (e.g., reordering commands to match required_sequence, splitting/normalizing command tokens). No multi-iteration repair or human escalation was allowed by design.

Inclusion, contamination, and missingness rules. The preregistered exclusion rules removed items failing deterministic vendor-parsers that prevented verification or items with detected credential-like tokens or denylist hits. Contamination detectors flagged instruction-like embedded tokens or private-address artifacts; flagged items would be excluded from primary analysis. The missingness plan specified one immediate retry on API failures and deterministic rules for treating incomplete calls; analysis sensitivity treatments were preregistered. In the executed confirmatory partition no episodes were excluded or flagged so the primary analysis used complete pairs only.

Analysis procedures. The primary analysis executor was paired_binary_analysis_v1. The primary test is an exact two-sided McNemar on paired binary outcomes; we also computed a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the guarded − baseline paired difference using 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). All analysis inputs, code, and outputs were archived.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and reconciliation. Execution completed the preregistered confirmatory partition with planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, and model_calls_used = 251. Provider-call auditing reconciles to 250 shared initial-generation calls and a single repair-stage generation (stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 250, repair = 1).

Primary binary outcomes and contingency. Deterministic validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency observations: n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair (baseline failed, guarded passed) corresponds to the only exercised repair call; repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition = 1/250 = 0.4%.

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided test on the discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returned p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the guarded − baseline paired difference (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] in proportion units (i.e., 0 – 1.2 percentage points). These numeric outputs are reproducible from the archived contingency table and analysis log.

Representative validator diagnostics and repair traces. Passed episodes show parsed_command_count equal to required_command_count per task; hard-difficulty tasks show higher parsed/required counts consistent with complex required_sequences. The single repair applied matched the preregistered, template-driven ordering correction and converted the candidate to validator-valid; all validator traces and the repair trace for that pair are archived for audit.

Missingness and contamination. No episodes were excluded and contamination detectors flagged no confirmatory episodes. Sensitivity analyses (planned) can treat hypothetical exclusions as failures; such sensitivity treatments are documented in the preregistration but were unnecessary for the executed run.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation partition, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the guarded pipeline converted the lone failing candidate via the single permitted repair. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) provides an empirical bound on the maximum plausible verifier-detected improvement under these pipeline and task constraints.

Artifact-grounded explanations. Three artifact-grounded factors explain the small observed gain: (1) the deterministic task generator encoded constrained intents and narrow allowed_touched_fields that reduced task ambiguity and favored well-formed CLI sequences; (2) the declared model produced highly consistent, syntactically well-formed sequences for these constrained intents; and (3) the deterministic validator measured mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, final_state snapshot) and therefore cannot capture broader behavioral correctness or emergent protocol-level interactions.

Power and assumptions. The preregistration power calculation assumed a baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 when selecting N_pairs = 250 to detect a 15 percentage-point absolute effect with ≈80% power. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) was substantially higher than assumed, reducing power to detect small absolute improvements; therefore the paired-bootstrap CI and the observed discordant counts are the most informative operational summaries for this study.

Threats to validity and scope. Internal validity: results depend on prompt templates, the single-repair policy, shared_initial_candidate semantics, and the precise validator encoding. Construct validity: the deterministic validator measures mechanically verifiable correctness (syntax, required_sequence, final_state snapshot) but does not assert live protocol-level correctness. External validity: the confirmatory evidence covers only the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed in this run. Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not exercised and remain an open threat.

Operational implications and caution. In tightly constrained emulation-style tasks with a capable LLM, a single validator+one-repair guardrail may yield small marginal verifier-detected benefit because initial candidates are already well-formed. This finding should not be generalized to broader operational contexts where task ambiguity, vendor heterogeneity, adversaries, or richer correctness criteria (protocol-level reachability, end-to-end service properties) may materially increase the utility of verification and richer repair workflows. Multi-iteration repair, richer validators, or human escalation could yield different operational benefits.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). We explicitly report that the preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast was not executed and that the executed confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on the synthetic/emulation partition only. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts referenced in this paper are archived in the submission evidence bundle for audit and reproducibility.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and performed pre-lock infrastructure development; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and framework: declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution used a guarded generate–verify–repair flow permitting at most one automated repair per episode as specified in the preregistration. Execution manifest reconciles planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, and model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial_generation + 1 repair).

Preregistration and immutable prompt references (archived): preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). Immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. All execution and analysis artifacts (raw model responses, task manifest, validator traces, repair traces, reconciliation and analysis artifacts) are archived in the submission evidence bundle accompanying this paper; the archived bundle contains the full manifests and per-artifact hashes for reproducibility and audit. 

Deviation disclosure: the preregistration included multiple partitions (synthetic/emulation, community, production-like) and a preregistered sim-to-real confirmatory contrast. The sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory comparison was not executed in this run; the reported confirmatory estimand and inference apply only to the synthetic/emulation partition (N_pairs = 250; shared_initial_candidate semantics).
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, final_state snapshot) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
